extracted.intended_audience: physicians, naturalists, and scientifically-interested general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting practical, taxonomic, and procedural guidance from a 19th-century popular-science/medical periodical containing articles for physicians, botanists, and engineers. The page collects multiple short pieces (natural history, medical therapeutics, instrument design, horticulture, geology, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaetophoraceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants growing in the sea or fresh water, coated by gelatinous substance; either filiform or a number of filaments being connected together constituting gelatinous, definitely formed, or shapeless fronds or masses. Filaments jointed, bearing bristle-like processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fructification: zoospores produced from the cell contents of the filaments; resting spores formed from the contents of particular cells after impregnation by ciliated spermatozoids produced in distinct antheridial cells. Example genus: Coleochætæ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confervaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants growing in the sea or in fresh water, filamentous, jointed, without evident gelatine (forming merely a delicate coat around the separate filaments). Filaments very variable in appearance, simple or branched; the cells constituting the articulations of the filaments more or less filled with green, or very rarely brown or purple granular matter; sometimes arranged in peculiar patterns on the walls, and convertible into spores or zoospores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not conjugating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zygnemaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Aquatic filamentous plants, without evident gelatine, composed of series of cylindrical cells, straight or curved. Cell contents often arranged in elegant patterns on the walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction resulting from conjugation, followed by the development of a true spore, in some genera dividing into four sporules before germinating.

rubrics_metrics.name: OEdogoniaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple or branched aquatic filamentous plants attached without gelatine. Cell contents uniform, dense, cell division accompanied by circumscissile debiscence of the parent cell, producing rings on the filaments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction by zoospores formed of the whole contents of a cell, with a crown of numerous cilia; resting spores formed in sporangial cells after fecundation by ciliated spermatozoids formed in antheridial cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Siphonaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants found in the sea, fresh water, or on damp ground; of a membranous or horny byaline substance, filled with green or colorless granular matter. Fronds consisting of continuous tubular filaments, either free or collected into spongy masses of various shapes. Crustaceous, globular, cylindrical, or flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fructification: by zoospores, either single or very numerous, and by resting spores formed in sporangial cells after the contents have been impregnated by the contents of antheridial cells of different forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oscillatoriaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants growing either in the sea, fresh water, or on damp ground, of a gelatinous substance and filamentous structure. Filaments very slender, tubular, continuous, filled with colored, granular, transversely striated substance; seldom blanched, though often cohering together so as to appear branched; usually massed together in broad floating or sessile strata, of a very gelatinous nature; occasionally erect and tufted, and still more rarely collected into radiating series bound together by firm gelatine and then forming globose lobed or flat crustaceous fronds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fructification: the internal mass or contents separating into roundish or lenticular gonidia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nostochacæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Gelatinous plants growing in fresh water, or in damp situations among mosses, etc.; of soft or almost leathery substance, consisting of variously curled or twisted necklace-shaped filaments, colorless or green, composed of simple, or in some stages double rows of cells, contained in a gelatinous matrix of definite form, or heaped together without order in a gelatinous mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of the cells enlarged, and then forming either vesicular empty cells or densely filled sporangial cells. Reproduction: by the breaking up of the filaments, and by resting spores formed singly in the sporanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ulvaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Marine or aquatic algae consisting of membranous, flat, and expanded tubular or saccate fronds composed of polygonal cells firmly joined together by their sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduced by zoospores formed from the cell contents and breaking out from the surface, or by motionless spores formed from the whole contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palmellaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants forming gelatinous or pulverulent crusts on damp surfaces of stone, wood, earth, mud, swampy districts, or more or less regular masses of gelatinous substance or delicate pseudo-membranous expansion or fronds, of flat, globular, or tubular form, in fresh water or on damp ground; composed of one or many, sometimes innumerable, cells, with green, red, or yellowish contents, spherical or elliptical form, the simplest being isolated cells found in groups of two, four, eight, etc., in course of multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction: by cell division, by the conversion of the cell contents into zoospores, and by resting spores, formed sometimes after conjugation; in other cases, probably, by fecundation by spermatozoids. All the unicellular algæ are included under this head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desmidiaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopic gelatinous plants, of a green color, growing in fresh water, composed of cells devoid of a silicious coat, of peculiar forms such as oval, crescentic, shortly cylindrical, cylindrical, oblong, etc., with variously formed rays or lobes, giving a more or less stellate form, presenting a bilateral symmetry, the junction of the halves being marked by a division of the green contents; the individual cells being free, or arranged in linear series, collected into fagot-like bundles or in elegant star like groups which are embedded in a common gelatinous coat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduced by division and by resting spores produced in sporangia formed after the conjugation of two cells and union of their contents, and by zoospores formed in the vegetative cells or in the germinating resting spores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diatomaceæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopic cellular bodies, growing in fresh, brackish, and sea water: free or attached, single, or embedded in gelatinous tubes, the individual cells (frustules) with yellowish or brown contents, and provided with a silicious coat composed of two usually symmetrical valves variously marked, with a connecting band or hoop at the suture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplied by division and by the formation of new larger individuals out of the contents of individual conjugated cells; perhaps also by spores and zoospores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volvocineæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopic cellular fresh water plants, composed of groups of bodies resembling zoospores connected into a definite form by their enveloping membranes. The families are formed either of assemblages of coated zoospores united in a definite form by the cohesion of their membranes, or assemblages of naked zoospores inclosed in a common investing membrane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The individual zoospore-like bodies, with two cilia throughout life, perforate the membranous coats, and by their conjoined action cause a free co-operative movement of the whole group. Reproduction by division, or by single cells being converted into new families; and by resting spores formed from some of the cells after impregnation by spermatozoids formed from the contents of other cells of the same family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ichthyol dermato-therapeutic usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ichthyol is a tar-like, vaseline-consistent substance obtained by distillation of bituminous substances and treatment with sulphuric acid; contains sulphur, oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and traces of phosphorus, and is comparable with a 10% sulphur salve but can be combined with lead and mercury preparations without decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical guidance from Dr. P. G. Unna: begin with a moderately strong preparation and reduce strength as treatment proceeds; moist eczema: start 20–30% reduced to 10%; papular conditions: 50% reduced to 20%; hands may require stronger than face; children weaker than adults; usable from 5% up to 40–50% or undiluted. Ichthyol mixes with vaseline, lard, or oil; partly soluble in alcohol/ether. Example formula for obstinate hand eczema: 'R. Lithargyri 10.0; coq.c. aceti, 30.0; ad reman. 20.0; adde olei olivar., adipis, aa 10.0; ichthyol 10.0, M. ft. ung.' Caution urged until internal effects are better known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autopsy table design specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of an improved autopsy table: top made of thick, heavy, cast glass concaved toward a central strainer opening; top approx. eight feet by two feet six inches; opening allows fluids to drain to waste pipe below to avoid soiling floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strainer has a downward draught passing through a large flue connected above the waste-trap to the boiler-house chimney to carry away offensive odors. Base includes a ground swinging attachment enabling rotation; cold and hot water supply cocks feed through a ball/swing joint under the plate glass top to a hose attachment for washing; ball swing permits turning without disturbing water connections. Table placed centrally in amphitheater so coroner's jury and officials can view the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oats excitant properties (avenine)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pericarp of oats contains a substance (called 'avenine') soluble in alcohol, nitrogenous (alkaloid-like), brown granular, uncrystallizable, which excites motor cells of the nervous system; all cultivated varieties produce it but in varying amounts depending on variety and place of cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical findings: less than 0.9% (per cent of air-dried oats) is insufficient to certainly affect horses; above this proportion excitant action is certain. Crushing/grinding weakens the excitant property (more prompt but less durable action). The isolated principle acts more immediate and intense. The effect rises to a peak then diminishes; total duration ~ one hour per kilogram of oats ingested. Determination of amount present is stated as the only sure basis of appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filaria disease pathology hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Manson's hypothesis for elephantoid lesions: a parent filaria in a distal lymphatic may abort and expel ova (rather than embryos); the ova, being larger, may embolize lymphatic passages and glands producing stasis, regurgitation of lymph, and compensatory anastomoses leading to tissue hypertrophy, lymphorrhoea or chyluria according to site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hypothesis is based on limited case observations (two cases cited) and is offered as a plausible explanation for elephantiasis, chyluria, and lymph scrotum. Additional observations include embryo and ovum dimensions and the possibility that parent-worm death in afferent lymphatics can cause abscesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masdevallia chimæra cultivation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Masdevallia (especially M. chimæra) typically comes from high altitudes and requires 'cool treatment' with abundant moisture both at the root and in the atmosphere; plants often push flowers at deflected angles and may be aided by support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivation suggestions: grow in shallow teak wood baskets suspended near the roof in partially shaded structures (better than pots or pans for chimæroid section); provide copious moisture and partial shade; prop up flowers with a stick for display/convenience (tails may need diagonal support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct re: new etiologic claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians should prioritize practical evidence and patient care over protracted taxonomic or nomenclatural disputes; if a clinician presents convincing etiologic evidence, practitioners ought to act on it without waiting for full agreement among naturalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be receptive to new truths even from less-established sources, avoid hasty denunciations, acknowledge limits of one's knowledge, examine offered evidence kindly and respectfully, and favor practical steps (warn, treat) over semantic or classificatory certainty when immediate health consequences are at stake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field collection and preservation methods for 'ague plants' (malarial algae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical observations for finding and preserving malaria plants: search bogs, pond-drippings, incrustations on soil, shaded ash piles, and sputa; plants may be found on various substrates and in environments not obviously marshy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preservation tip: wind a wet bandage around the slide to keep plants in good condition until examination. Instructing and training a lay collector (patient) in simple microscopy collection techniques can yield specimens. Macroscopic examination may be insufficient; microscopic search of sputa, urine, blood, and collected films may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed survey/engineering method for Black Cañon
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested approach for surveying through the heavy portion of the Black Canon of the Gunnison for a railroad: build a boat at the western end and provision it for a length of time to float with the stream while controlled by ropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If boat method succeeds, the Denver and Rio Grande line may be built through the cañon; the proposal notes the river is very swift and that for many miles the walls arch closely over the river bed, implying significant engineering challenges.
